2607.16716.title: RECON: Benchmarking Agent Memory for Compositional Reasoning over Long Contexts
2607.16716.paper_summary: Large language models and LLM-based agents are widely used as personal chat assistants, enterprise copilots, and autonomous workflow agents. In all these applications, memory (the ability to retain, access, and reason over information accumulated over long contexts and multiple interactions) plays a crucial role in determining the reliability of any agent. We introduce RECON (Reasoning over Extended Contexts with Obfuscated Narratives), a benchmark for evaluating compositional reasoning over long contexts. RECON spans 24 case files across three domains (criminal, medical, and financial), each ranging from 50k to 100k tokens, and tests agents on six memory intensive tasks: reconstructing multi-hop evidence chains, propagating cascading invalidations, resolving source conflicts, counterfactual reasoning, satisfying temporal constraints, and temporal fact retrieval. Recent memory benchmarks evaluate whether agents can retrieve scattered facts or detect if a fact has changed whereas RECON evaluates what happens after the change, whether agents can trace which downstream conclusions are affected, which survive through independent support, and how alternative timelines would have unfolded. Our evaluation reveals substantial limitations across current architectures: even the strongest non-Oracle system reaches only 22.4% Accuracy, with retrieval and reasoning each surfacing as challenges.
2607.16716.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型和基於LLM的代理被廣泛用作個人聊天助手、企業副駕駛和自主工作流程代理。<lb/>在所有這些應用中，記憶（保留、訪問和推理長期上下文和多次互動中積累的信息的能力）在決定任何代理的可靠性方面扮演著至關重要的角色。<lb/>我們介紹RECON（基於模糊敘事的擴展上下文推理），這是一個用於評估長期上下文中組合推理的基準。<lb/>RECON涵蓋了三個領域（刑事、醫療和金融）中的24個案例文件，每個案例的字元數範圍從50k到100k，並在六個記憶密集型任務上測試代理：重建多跳證據鏈、傳播級聯無效、解決來源衝突、反事實推理、滿足時間約束和時間事實檢索。<lb/>最近的記憶基準評估代理是否能夠檢索分散的事實或檢測事實是否已經改變，而RECON則評估變更後發生了什麼，代理是否能夠追蹤哪些下游結論受到影響，哪些通過獨立支持得以生存，以及替代時間線將如何展開。<lb/>我們的評估揭示了當前架構的重大限制：即使是最強的非Oracle系統也僅達到22.4%的準確率，檢索和推理各自都成為挑戰。
